separation_rule: This file contains shared guidance only. User facts, uploads, extracts and drafts belong in the private case workspace and must never be inserted here.

questions.prompt: What did you buy, and was it mainly for personal use?
questions.why: Tests whether the supported consumer workflow may fit without assuming consumer status.

questions.prompt: Who sold it, and was a marketplace or payment intermediary involved?
questions.why: Identifies the possible opposite parties and available records.

questions.prompt: When did you order and pay?
questions.why: Starts the chronology and timing review.

questions.prompt: Was it delivered, cancelled, returned, or never delivered? When?
questions.why: Separates non-delivery, cancellation, return, defect and refund paths.
Identifies the factual issue without converting it into a legal conclusion.

questions.prompt: What did the seller or platform say about the refund, return, repair or replacement?
questions.why: Captures stated commitments and their source.

questions.prompt: What have you already sent or done, and what response did you receive?
questions.why: Avoids repeating completed steps and preserves correspondence history.

questions.prompt: What outcome do you want now: refund, repair, replacement, delivery, or something else?
questions.why: Keeps the requested remedy separate from possible legal relief.

questions.prompt: Which documents, messages, photographs or transaction records do you have?
questions.why: Builds an evidence checklist and identifies material gaps.

branches.reason: Do not assume the seller never initiated a refund; distinguish initiation, routing and receipt.
Marketplace, seller and platform records may support different facts.
A purchase record alone does not establish a defect or its cause.
Separates dispatch, attempted delivery, misdelivery and non-dispatch.
Consumer status may require legal assessment and must not be assumed.
Keep one case per chat without forcing separation.

questions.prompt: What is the product, model and serial number if available?
questions.why: Connects the complaint to the correct goods and records.

questions.prompt: What condition, feature or quality was advertised or promised?
questions.why: Creates a comparison point without assuming a legal breach.

questions.prompt: What did you personally observe, and when?
questions.why: Separates observation from inference about cause.

questions.prompt: How was it used, stored and handled before the problem appeared?
questions.why: Identifies possible factual objections and preservation needs.

questions.prompt: Has the seller, manufacturer or an independent technician inspected it?
questions.why: Identifies expert or service evidence and conflicting explanations.

branches.reason: Record the objection and evidence instead of treating either account as established.
Prioritise safety and professional help where needed.

questions.prompt: What delivery date or range was promised, and where is it recorded?
What does the complete tracking history show?
questions.why: Separates non-dispatch, transit delay, attempted delivery and delivered-status disputes.

questions.prompt: Was the delivery address correct in the order confirmation?
Has the seller or carrier provided delivery proof, a recipient name or location?
questions.why: Identifies evidence that may conflict with the user's account.

branches.reason: A delivered scan and actual receipt are distinct facts.

evidence_playbooks.request: Complete invoice/order confirmation showing seller, product, amount and date.
common_contradictions: invoice seller differs from platform name
invoice date differs from payment date
evidence_playbooks.preservation: Keep the original file or email and export a copy without editing it.

evidence_playbooks.request: Payment confirmation or bank/card/UPI entry with sensitive unrelated entries redacted where possible.
does_not_automatically_prove: the payment was never reversed elsewhere
evidence_playbooks.preservation: Preserve the original statement and note any redactions made for sharing.

evidence_playbooks.request: Complete conversation or email thread including sender, date and surrounding messages.
common_contradictions: seller and platform give different accounts
evidence_playbooks.preservation: Keep the original message export or email headers; do not rely only on a cropped screenshot.

evidence_playbooks.request: Original photographs or video showing the product, serial number, packaging and observed problem.
evidence_playbooks.preservation: Keep original files and avoid filters, annotations or recompression of the only copy.

evidence_playbooks.request: Complete email, ticket or letter requesting the refund, plus any delivery or acknowledgement record.
evidence_playbooks.preservation: Keep the sent-message original and server acknowledgement where available.

evidence_playbooks.request: Statement covering the claimed refund window and relevant account or instrument.
may_support: transactions shown during the supplied period
absence of an obvious matching credit in that period
does_not_automatically_prove: that a pending or reversed credit never existed
common_contradictions: refund sent to original card not bank account
partial credit under a processor name
evidence_playbooks.preservation: Keep the original downloaded statement; redact unrelated transactions only in the sharing copy.

evidence_playbooks.request: Complete report including technician identity, date, tests and conclusion.
common_contradictions: seller report and independent report disagree
evidence_playbooks.preservation: Keep the signed original and any photographs or readings supplied with it.

procedures.title: Factual seller or platform request
procedures.when_may_fit: The person wants to clarify facts, invoke a stated policy or request a remedy before escalation.
procedures.authority: Seller, service provider, marketplace or grievance officer
instructions: State facts and sources separately from legal conclusions.
Attach copies, not the only originals.
Request acknowledgement and retain the complete sent record.
procedures.what_happens_next: The recipient may accept, reject, request more information or not respond; record the actual outcome before choosing another step.
procedures.limitations: No universal pre-action notice or response period is asserted. Any period stated in a draft must be labelled as requested unless a cited rule supplies it.

procedures.title: National Consumer Helpline pre-litigation grievance
procedures.when_may_fit: A consumer wants a government-supported pre-litigation grievance channel and understands that resolution is not guaranteed.
procedures.authority: National Consumer Helpline, Department of Consumer Affairs
instructions: Keep the docket or grievance number.
Record company responses and the outcome.
procedures.what_happens_next: NCH forwards the grievance through its convergence process; an unresolved person may consider the appropriate Consumer Commission or professional advice.
procedures.limitations: NCH describes itself as pre-litigation and does not guarantee a remedy. Operational details can change.

procedures.title: Consumer Commission complaint through current official platform
procedures.when_may_fit: A person is considering adjudication and needs forum, territorial jurisdiction, monetary jurisdiction, limitation, pleadings, evidence, fee and service reviewed.
procedures.authority: Appropriate District, State or National Consumer Commission
required_inputs: timing and delay explanation if relevant
instructions: Verify current e-Jagriti instructions and accepted formats at filing time.
Prepare a chronology, party details, relief, evidence index and source-backed legal issues.
Check current fee, signature, affidavit, service and copy requirements rather than relying on an old tutorial.
procedures.what_happens_next: The Commission may examine admissibility, issue notice, receive the opposite party's response, consider evidence, refer a suitable dispute to mediation, hear the matter and pass an order; actual stages vary.
procedures.limitations: This playbook does not select a forum from similarity alone and does not file or serve anything.

procedures.title: Consumer mediation after Commission consideration
procedures.when_may_fit: A consumer dispute is pending before a Commission, appears suitable for settlement and is not within a statutory exclusion.
procedures.authority: Consumer mediation cell attached to the relevant Commission
instructions: Check Rule 4 exclusions and current Commission procedure.
Keep hypothetical settlement ranges separate from admissions.
Have any settlement wording reviewed before acceptance where consequences are material.
procedures.what_happens_next: Suitability and referral are controlled by the Commission; settlement consequences depend on the governing procedure.
procedures.limitations: Mediation is not automatically available or appropriate and is not a guaranteed settlement.

selected_judgments.case_name: Experion Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. Sushma Ashok Shiroor
selected_judgments.material_facts: Homebuyer refund dispute concerning delayed apartment possession, one-sided agreement terms and overlapping Consumer Protection Act 1986 and RERA remedies.
issues: consumer commission power to direct refund
selected_judgments.holding_summary: On its facts, the Supreme Court upheld the refund direction and explained that the consumer and RERA remedies considered there did not exclude each other.
selected_judgments.exact_excerpt: the Commission has the power and jurisdiction to direct return of money
important_distinctions: high-value delayed possession rather than retail goods
selected_judgments.treatment_status: Supreme Court final judgment; subsequent treatment not independently checked
selected_judgments.use_rule: May identify arguments or distinctions. Must not be presented as promising the same result in a retail refund case.
